ing: long, mild to medium, such as Anaheim, sliced lengthwise
st: Slice the chilies lengthwise and remove the seeds for less heat.
Melt [[2 tbsp]] butter in a pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and garlic and cook 3 minutes until soft.
Add the chilies, tomatoes, [[1 cup]] water and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Cover and simmer 10 minutes until the chilies are tender.
Crumble [[8 oz]] cheese over the top, cover, and cook 5 minutes without stirring.
Stir gently until the cheese melts into a thick, creamy sauce.
Taste and adjust salt, then serve hot with red rice or white rice.
Peel the potatoes and slice them about 1/4 inch thick.
Melt [[2 tbsp]] butter in a pot. Cook the onion and garlic for 3 minutes.
Add the potatoes, chilies, tomato, [[1.5 cups]] water and [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Cover and simmer 15 minutes until the potatoes are just tender.
Crumble [[6 oz]] cheese into the pot.
Cover and cook 5 minutes over low heat. Stir gently until the sauce is creamy, without breaking the potatoes.
Serve hot with red or white rice.
Clean the mushrooms with a damp cloth and slice them.
Melt [[2 tbsp]] butter in a skillet over medium heat.
Cook the onion and garlic for 3 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and cook 6 minutes until they release their water and brown a little.
Add the chilies, [[0.5 cup]] water and [[0.5 tsp]] salt, cover, and simmer 5 minutes.
Crumble in [[6 oz]] cheese and cook covered 4 minutes.
Stir until the cheese melts into a sauce and serve with rice.
Peel the radish and slice it into thin half-moons.
Put the pork belly in a pot with [[1 cup]] water and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Simmer covered 20 minutes.
Uncover and cook until the water evaporates and the fat renders, about 8 minutes. Add [[1 tbsp]] oil if the pan is dry.
Brown the pork 4 to 5 minutes, stirring now and then.
Add the ginger, garlic, onion and dried chilies and stir-fry 3 minutes.
Add the radish and [[0.5 tsp]] salt and stir for 2 minutes.
Cover and cook on low 10 minutes until the radish is tender and the pork reaches 145°F (63°C) or more.
Top with the green onions and serve with rice.
Mix [[3 cups]] flour and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Add warm water slowly, about [[1 cup]], and knead 8 minutes into a firm dough.
Cover and rest the dough for 30 minutes.
Mix the beef, cabbage, onion, garlic, ginger, [[1 tsp]] salt, pepper and [[1 tbsp]] oil in a bowl. Add the optional cheese.
Roll the dough into a log and cut into 24 pieces.
Roll each piece into a thin 3-inch circle, thinner at the edges.
Put a spoonful of filling in the center and pleat the edges to seal at the top.
Oil a steamer basket and arrange the momos without touching.
Steam over boiling water 15 minutes until the beef reaches 160°F (71°C) and the dough looks glossy.
Serve hot with chili sauce.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a pot over medium heat.
Cook the onion, garlic and ginger for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the ground chicken, break it up well, and cook 6 minutes until it is no longer pink.
Add the tomatoes, chilies and [[1 tsp]] salt and cook 6 minutes until the tomatoes collapse.
Pour in [[1 cup]] water, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Uncover and cook 3 more minutes to thicken the stew.
Stir in the cilantro and serve with rice.
Bring [[2 cups]] water to a boil and add [[1 tbsp]] tea leaves.
Simmer 5 minutes so the tea turns dark and strong.
Strain the tea into a blender or tall jar.
Add [[2 tbsp]] butter, [[0.25 cup]] milk, optional [[2 tbsp]] cream and [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Blend on low (hold the lid down tightly on hot liquid) or whisk hard for 30 seconds until frothy and creamy.
Pour into cups and serve hot.
